title: Range queries: Fenwick, segtree, sparse table (Depth Pass)
relevance: High (second ladder after CSES/EDU templates — CF Div2 C–E “rewrite the ask into a merge / walk / offline count,” GCD-sparse tricks, and custom node structs that still appear as hard OA twists)
company_notes: Coverage scheduling: each query marks a range; assign priorities/values to maximize sum — Little Girl / difference-array frequency. Unique/distinct in window: distinct SKUs on [l,r] — Distinct Values / last-occurrence Fenwick. Custom aggregate API: max subarray sum after point edits or count of second-max in a segment — Subarray Sum Queries / Second Largest Query. Pair/subsequence counting under order constraints: increasing length-k / dominance pairs — Subsequences / Jealous Two.

phases.goal: Spot when range DS stops being a pasted template and needs custom merge, offline Fenwick, or sparse+pointers.

must_hit.point: After Dynamic Range Sum / Hotel Queries / Sereja-and-Brackets-classics, contest range DS requires inventing what each node stores (max subarray, top-2, GCD+count), running Fenwick offline over sorted endpoints, or pairing a sparse table with two pointers / binary lifting on idempotent ops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names custom node contents, offline Fenwick over endpoints, or sparse+two-pointers/binary lifting instead of pasting a basic template.

must_hit.point: Recognize it when many [l,r] asks survive only if you pre-merge associative info, when updates are rare-but-heavy (digit-sum, D(n)), or when the answer is a count of pairs/subsequences that a frequency BIT can accumulate while sweeping.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites pre-merge associative info, rare-but-heavy updates, or sweeping frequency-BIT pair/subsequence counts as the cue.

must_hit.point: OA wording maps to coverage scheduling (Little Girl), distinct SKUs in [l,r] (Distinct Values), custom aggregates like max subarray / second-max (Subarray Sum Queries / Second Largest Query), or order-constrained pair counts (Subsequences / Jealous Two).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties one of those OA shapes to the matching depth-pass pattern.

probes: What in the statement says this is custom merge, offline Fenwick, or sparse+pointers rather than paste Dynamic Range Sum / basic PURS?
Is the ask many [l,r] associative merges, rare-but-heavy digit-sum/D(n) updates, or a sweeping pair/subsequence count?

hints.1: Ask whether a pasted Fenwick/segtree sum node is enough, or the node/query model must be invented.
hints.2: Signals: invent node fields; offline sorted endpoints; sparse+two pointers on idempotent ops; rare-but-heavy replace; frequency BIT while sweeping.
hints.3: Say: pre-merge associative info / offline Fenwick / sparse+pointers; OA cousins are coverage assign, distinct in window, max-subarray or second-max API, and dominance / length-k subsequence counts.

phases.goal: Choose the right depth model: coverage rearrange, GCD prune, offline last-occurrence, dual affine mins, layered BIT DP, sparse+pointers, stable replace, or custom merge.

must_hit.point: Coverage → rearrange: build range “+1 usefulness” via difference array, then greedily assign largest values to most-queried indices (Little Girl and Maximum Sum).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds per-index query frequency with a difference array and assigns largest a_i to hottest indices.

must_hit.point: Offline last-occurrence: sort queries by r, walk i=1..n, add(prev[a_i],-1), add(i,+1), answer distinct on [l,r] as sum(r)-sum(l-1) (Distinct Values Queries).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts by r, maintains last occurrence on a Fenwick, and answers with two prefix sums.

must_hit.point: Dual affine trees: pizza cost |x-i|+a_i rewrites as query min(a_i-i)+x left of x and min(a_i+i)-x right — two point-update range-min segtrees (Pizzeria Queries).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Folds ±i into stored values and answers left/right range mins independently.

must_hit.point: GCD segtree prune: if node_gcd % x == 0 skip; else recurse — with at most one “bad” child you get near-O(log n) replace/check (Bash and a Tough Math Puzzle).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Skips divisible GCD nodes and relies on at most one bad child for early exit.

must_hit.point: Layered BIT DP: dp[k][i] = sum dp[k-1][j] over a_j < a_i via Fenwick on value; k trees or one reused layer (Subsequences).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Accelerates increasing-subsequence DP layers with Fenwick on compressed values.

must_hit.point: Sparse + monotonic pointers: for each L, grow R while gcd(L..R) (or max-min) still satisfies a predicate — each endpoint moves O(n) total (Array Stabilization / Friends and Subsequences).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Pairs sparse RMQ/GCD with two pointers so endpoints move O(n) total.

must_hit.point: 2D / dominance: sort one axis, Fenwick the other (Jealous Two, Box in Box, Tufurama).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts one constraint and BIT-queries the other for dominance/pair counts.

probes: Do you rearrange by coverage frequency, answer offline by r, rewrite distance as a_i±i mins, or prune a GCD segtree?
When is the model layered BIT DP, sparse+two pointers, or sort-one-axis Fenwick-the-other?

hints.1: Match the ask to one non-obvious trick, not a generic PURS template.
hints.2: Diff coverage+sort; offline last-occurrence; dual a_i±i mins; GCD prune; k-layer BIT DP; sparse+pointers; sort+BIT dominance.
hints.3: Say: Little Girl diff+assign; Distinct Values sort-by-r last-occurrence; Pizzeria two affine mins; Bash GCD prune; Subsequences layered BIT; Array Stabilization/Friends sparse+pointers; Jealous Two/Box/Tufurama sort+BIT.

phases.goal: Encode custom merge nodes, offline Fenwick bookkeeping, stable-range skips, and Fenwick walk/binary-lift restores.

must_hit.point: Custom merge beyond sum/min: node = (total, pref, suf, best) for max subarray, or (mx, mx_cnt, second, second_cnt) for second-largest frequency — merge is pure casework on the two children.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the four-field max-subarray merge or top-2-with-freq casework merge.

must_hit.point: For max-subarray merge nodes, empty subarray allowed ⇒ best≥0 (Subarray Sum Queries / GSS1-style).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Forces best to be at least 0 when empty subarray is allowed.

must_hit.point: “Replace until stable” segtree: store range max; if max ≤ 2 (or digit-sum fixed point) skip; else point-update children — total updates O(n log A) (SUM and REPLACE / Range Update Point Query).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Skips stable segments via range max (or digit-sum fixed points) and only updates children that can still change.

must_hit.point: Walk/binary-lift on Fenwick prefix sums restores permutations and finds k-th remaining (Restore Permutation / Multiset family).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Binary-lifts on BIT prefix sums to locate the needed remaining value/position.

must_hit.point: Range Update Point Query digit-sum ops: values stabilize ≤9; maintain “still large” indices in a set / segtree and skip fixed points.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Tracks only indices still above the digit-sum fixed point and skips the rest.

probes: What fields does your merge node need for max subarray vs second-largest frequency, and how do you merge two children?
How do you skip stable replace segments, and when do you binary-lift on a Fenwick prefix sum?

hints.1: Write the node struct and the skip/walk mechanics before coding the whole tree.
hints.2: (sum,pref,suf,best) with best≥0 if empty allowed; top-2 freqs; skip when max≤2 or digit-sum fixed; BIT binary-lift for k-th remaining.
hints.3: Say: GSS1-style four-tuple with best≥0; Second Largest top-2+counts; SUM and REPLACE skip max≤2 with O(n log A) potential; Restore Permutation binary-lift on BIT; digit-sum stabilize ≤9 with a set of still-large indices.

phases.goal: Explain why offline sweeps, sparse+pointers, and stable-range early exits beat naive per-query full scans.

must_hit.point: Idempotent static ops (min/max/GCD) → sparse table; then two-pointer / BS on endpoints is O(n log) or O(n), not O(n²).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States sparse for idempotent ops and endpoint search as O(n log) or O(n), not O(n²).

must_hit.point: Early-exit / “stable range” updates: if the aggregate already implies no change, do not push into children — complexity comes from potential, not from q log n worst-case alone.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Attributes cost to a potential/early-exit argument rather than claiming every query is full tree work.

must_hit.point: Sparse + monotonic pointers: each endpoint moves O(n) total when growing R under a GCD or max-min predicate.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says each endpoint moves O(n) total across the two-pointer sweep.

must_hit.point: GCD segtree prune with at most one bad child yields near-O(log n) replace/check.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites the at-most-one-bad-child prune for near-O(log n) behavior.

probes: Why is sparse+two-pointers not O(n²) on endpoint searches?
Where does the cost of replace-until-stable or GCD-prune actually come from?

hints.1: Separate static idempotent queries from update-heavy replace loops.
hints.2: Sparse then O(n log)/O(n) endpoint motion; stable ranges charged to potential not q log n alone; GCD prune near-O(log n).
hints.3: Say: idempotent → sparse + two-pointer/BS is O(n log) or O(n), not O(n²); skip when aggregate implies no change (potential, not q log n alone); endpoints O(n) total; Bash prune near-O(log n).

phases.goal: Catch compression, overflow, incomplete node fields, and missing offline/early-exit bookkeeping.

must_hit.point: Always compress before BIT when values/pref hit 10^9; keep long long for sums and XOR-of-sums mixes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compresses large values/prefixes and uses long long for sum and XOR mixes.

must_hit.point: Node design checklist failure: missing fields so children cannot merge (need sum+pref+suf+best; gcd; top-2; OR of bits; or min with index as required).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists which fields are necessary for the asked merge and notices a missing one.

must_hit.point: Answering commuting [l,r] distinct/pair queries online when offline > online: should sort by r (or by value), Fenwick the sweeping side, and answer in input order via ids.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts commuting queries, sweeps with Fenwick, and restores input order by ids.

must_hit.point: Pushing into children on a stable range whose aggregate already implies no change (max≤2 / digit-sum fixed point / node_gcd divisible).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Skips recursion when the node aggregate already proves the update/check is done.

probes: What breaks if you BIT raw 10^9 values, or merge max-subarray with only a sum field?
When should you refuse to recurse into children, and when should queries be answered offline?

hints.1: Depth bugs are missing compression, merge fields, or early-exit/offline discipline.
hints.2: Compress at 10^9; long long for sums/XOR mixes; enough merge fields; offline sort-by-r; skip stable aggregates.
hints.3: Say: compress before BIT at 10^9 and use long long; design sum+pref+suf+best / top-2 / gcd fields; offline when queries commute; do not push if max≤2, digit-sum fixed, or gcd already divisible.

tradeoffs.topic: Offline vs online when queries commute
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Offline > online when queries commute: sort by r (or by value), Fenwick the sweeping side, answer in input order via ids (Distinct Values / last-occurrence family).

tradeoffs.topic: Sparse table vs segtree for idempotent static ops
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Idempotent static ops (min/max/GCD) → sparse table; then two-pointer / BS on endpoints is O(n log) or O(n), not O(n²) — prefer this over a segtree when there are no updates.

tradeoffs.topic: Custom merge node vs sum/min-only tree
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When the API needs max subarray or second-largest frequency, store (total, pref, suf, best) or (mx, mx_cnt, second, second_cnt) and merge by casework — a sum/min-only node cannot answer.

tradeoffs.topic: Dual affine range-mins vs searching |x-i|+a_i directly
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Fold ±i into the stored value so plain range-min answers best index near x: query min(a_i-i)+x left and min(a_i+i)-x right with two PUR-min segtrees (Pizzeria Queries).

tradeoffs.topic: Early-exit stable-range updates vs touching the whole segment every time
tradeoffs.strong_answer: If the aggregate already implies no change (max≤2, digit-sum fixed point, node_gcd % x == 0), do not push into children; complexity comes from potential, not from q log n worst-case alone.
For 2D / dominance pair counts, sort one axis and Fenwick the other (Jealous Two, Box in Box, Tufurama) rather than building a full 2D tree when one dimension can be swept.

gotchas.trap: BIT on raw values/prefixes that hit 10^9, or int sums for large aggregates / XOR-of-sums mixes.
gotchas.correction: Always compress before BIT when values/pref hit 10^9; keep long long for sums and XOR-of-sums mixes.

gotchas.trap: Max-subarray merge that forbids the empty subarray when the problem allows it.
gotchas.correction: Empty subarray allowed ⇒ best≥0 (Subarray Sum Queries / GSS1-style).

gotchas.trap: Answering distinct-on-[l,r] with Mo or online structure when last-occurrence offline Fenwick fits.
gotchas.correction: Sort queries by r, walk i=1..n with add(prev[a_i],-1), add(i,+1), answer sum(r)-sum(l-1).

gotchas.trap: Range digit-sum / D(n) replace that updates every index every time.
gotchas.correction: Values stabilize ≤9 (digit-sum) or skip segments with max≤2 (SUM and REPLACE); maintain still-large indices and charge updates to O(n log A) potential.

gotchas.trap: GCD divisibility replace/check that always recurses into both children.
gotchas.correction: If node_gcd % x == 0 skip; else recurse — at most one bad child gives near-O(log n) (Bash and a Tough Math Puzzle).

gotchas.trap: Pizza / distance cost answered by scanning neighbors of x.
gotchas.correction: Rewrite |x-i|+a_i as left min(a_i-i)+x and right min(a_i+i)-x on two point-update range-min segtrees.

gotchas.trap: Node that stores only sum/min when the ask needs second-max frequency or max subarray.
gotchas.correction: Use (mx, mx_cnt, second, second_cnt) or (total, pref, suf, best) and merge by casework on the two children.
